blockers.quote: Four per cent of everyone in the country who sat it (c01).
blockers.why: Overstates the scope of row c01 and violates the digits-mean-facts convention. The verbatim quote in c01 specifies that 'Except for the English and Korean-history sections, grades are based on a stanine curve', and the ledger note cautions that 'Most subjects', not every subject, follow the 4% cut-off. Line 284 drops this limitation and asserts a universal 4% curve. Additionally, the real-world finding is written as a word ('Four per cent') rather than using digits ('4 per cent') citing its row inline.
blockers.fix: In most subjects, the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it (c01).

keep.quote: Envy comes in two kinds (c07). One pushes you to move up. The other pushes you to pull the other person down (c07).
In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain (c05).
At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver (c08). Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing (c08).
